current_example.title: Example: Solving a Singular 2x2 System of Equations Using Gaussian Elimination

q-73743.name: Question 1
q-73743.problem:
Consider the augmented matrix $M$ given by 

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}3 & -2 & 1 \\ 6 & -4 & 2\end{aligned}].
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce $M$ to row echelon form.
q-73743.worked_solution:
Reducing $M$ to echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}3 & -2 & 1 \\ 6 & -4 & 2\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=\frac{1}{3}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -\frac{2}{3} & \frac{1}{3} \\ 6 & -4 & 2\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}-6{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -\frac{2}{3} & \frac{1}{3} \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

q-73524.name: Question 2
q-73524.problem:
Consider the augmented matrix $M$ given by 

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}4 & -16 & 8 \\ -3 & 12 & -6\end{aligned}].
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce $M$ to row echelon form.
q-73524.worked_solution:
Reducing $M$ to echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}4 & -16 & 8 \\ -3 & 12 & -6\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=\frac{1}{4}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -4 & 2 \\ -3 & 12 & -6\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+3{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -4 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

q-20782.name: Question 3
q-20782.problem:
Consider the augmented matrix $M$ given by 

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & -3 \\ -7 & 14 & 21\end{aligned}].
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce $M$ to row echelon form, and then find the general solution of the linear system represented by the matrix.
q-20782.worked_solution:
Reducing $M$ to echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & -3 \\ -7 & 14 & 21\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+7{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & -3 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

The corresponding system is now

$$
{\begin{aligned}x-2y=-3 \\ 0x+0y=0.\end{aligned}
$$

Since any pair of numbers $x,y$ is a solution of the final equation $0x+0y=0,$ we can remove this equation from the system. So, our system now consists of a single equation

$$
x-2y=-3.
$$

The first variable $(x)$ is the basic variable, and the second variable $(y)$ is the free variable. Solving for the basic variable $(x)$ in terms of the free variable $(y),$ we get $x=-3+2y,$ and the general solution is

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=-3+2y \\ y=y\end{aligned}
$$

where $y$ is an arbitrary number. 

In vector form, the general solution can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-3+2y \\ y\end{aligned}],\,y\in (-\infty ,\infty ).\end{aligned}
$$

Question 3
?

Consider the augmented matrix M given by M=[1−2−3−71421].

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce M to row echelon form, and then find the general solution of the linear system represented by the matrix.

a
[xy]=[−2+3yy],y∈(−∞,∞)
b
[xy]=[3+2yy],y∈(−∞,∞)
c
[xy]=[3−2yy],y∈(−∞,∞)
d
[xy]=[−3+2yy],y∈(−∞,∞)
e
[xy]=[−3−2yy],y∈(−∞,∞)
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

Reducing M to echelon form, we have

M∼[1−2−3−71421]R2:=R2+7R1∼[1−2−3000].

The corresponding system is now

{x−2y=−30x+0y=0.

Since any pair of numbers x,y is a solution of the final equation 0x+0y=0, we can remove this equation from the system. So, our system now consists of a single equation

x−2y=−3.

The first variable (x) is the basic variable, and the second variable (y) is the free variable. Solving for the basic variable (x) in terms of the free variable (y), we get x=−3+2y, and the general solution is

{x=−3+2yy=y

where y is an arbitrary number.

In vector form, the general solution can be written as [xy]=[−3+2yy],y∈(−∞,∞).

q-73741.name: Question 4
q-73741.problem:
Consider the augmented matrix $M$ given by 

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}2 & 4 & -2 \\ -5 & -10 & 5\end{aligned}].
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce $M$ to row echelon form.
q-73741.worked_solution:
Reducing $M$ to echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 4 & -2 \\ -5 & -10 & 5\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=\frac{1}{2}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & -1 \\ -5 & -10 & 5\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+5{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

q-42155.name: Question 5
q-42155.problem:
Consider the augmented matrix $M$ given by 

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 3 \\ -3 & 3 & -9\end{aligned}].
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce $M$ to row echelon form, and then find the general solution of the linear system represented by the matrix.
q-42155.worked_solution:
Reducing $M$ to echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 3 \\ -3 & 3 & -9\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+3{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

The corresponding system is now

$$
{\begin{aligned}x-y=3 \\ 0x+0y=0.\end{aligned}
$$

Since any pair of numbers $x,y$ is a solution of the final equation $0x+0y=0,$ we can remove this equation from the system. So, our system now consists of a single equation

$$
x-y=3.
$$

The first variable $(x)$ is the basic variable, and the second variable $(y)$ is the free variable. Solving for the basic variable $(x)$ in terms of the free variable $(y),$ we get $x=3+y,$ and the general solution is

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=3+y \\ y=y\end{aligned}
$$

where $y$ is an arbitrary number. 

In vector form, the general solution can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}3+y \\ y\end{aligned}],\,y\in (-\infty ,\infty ).\end{aligned}
$$

Question 5
?

Consider the augmented matrix M given by M=[1−13−33−9].

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce M to row echelon form, and then find the general solution of the linear system represented by the matrix.

a
[xy]=[1+yy],y∈(−∞,∞)
b
[xy]=[−3−yy],y∈(−∞,∞)
c
[xy]=[−3+yy],y∈(−∞,∞)
d
[xy]=[3−yy],y∈(−∞,∞)
e
[xy]=[3+yy],y∈(−∞,∞)
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Reducing M to echelon form, we have

M=[1−13−33−9]R2:=R2+3R1∼[1−13000].

The corresponding system is now

{x−y=30x+0y=0.

Since any pair of numbers x,y is a solution of the final equation 0x+0y=0, we can remove this equation from the system. So, our system now consists of a single equation

x−y=3.

The first variable (x) is the basic variable, and the second variable (y) is the free variable. Solving for the basic variable (x) in terms of the free variable (y), we get x=3+y, and the general solution is

{x=3+yy=y

where y is an arbitrary number.

In vector form, the general solution can be written as [xy]=[3+yy],y∈(−∞,∞).

q-42157.name: Question 6
q-42157.problem:
Consider the system of linear equations

$$
{\begin{aligned}x-6y=2 \\ -4x+24y=-10.\end{aligned}
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to row echelon form, and then find the general solution of the linear system.
q-42157.worked_solution:
First, we set up the augmented matrix for the system:

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}1 & -6 & 2 \\ -4 & 24 & -10\end{aligned}]
$$

Reducing $M$ to row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -6 & 2 \\ -4 & 24 & -10\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+4{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -6 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & -2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

The corresponding system is now

$$
{\begin{aligned}x-6y=2 \\ 0x+0y=-2.\end{aligned}
$$

However, the final equation $0x+0y=-2$ has no solution. It simplifies to $0=-2,$ which is a false statement.

So, there is no pair $x,y$ that satisfies both equations in the system. Consequently, the overall system has no solution.

q-42154.name: Question 7
q-42154.problem:
Consider the system of linear equations

$$
{\begin{aligned}3x+9y=12 \\ 4x+12y=13.\end{aligned}
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to row echelon form, and then find the general solution of the linear system.
q-42154.worked_solution:
First, we set up the augmented matrix for the system:

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}3 & 9 & 12 \\ 4 & 12 & 13\end{aligned}]
$$

Reducing $M$ to row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}3 & 9 & 12 \\ 4 & 12 & 13\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=\frac{1}{3}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 4 \\ 4 & 12 & 13\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}-4{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 4 \\ 0 & 0 & -3\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

The corresponding system is now

$$
{\begin{aligned}x+3y=4 \\ 0x+0y=-3.\end{aligned}
$$

However, the final equation $0x+0y=-3$ has no solution. It simplifies to $0=-3,$ which is a false statement.

So, there is no pair $x,y$ that satisfies both equations in the system. Consequently, the overall system has no solution.

q-73749.name: Question 8
q-73749.problem:
Consider the system of linear equations

$$
{\begin{aligned}x+3y=1 \\ 2x+6y=3.\end{aligned}
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to row echelon form, and then find the general solution of the linear system.
q-73749.worked_solution:
First, we set up the augmented matrix for the system:

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 1 \\ 2 & 6 & 3\end{aligned}]
$$

Reducing $M$ to row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 1 \\ 2 & 6 & 3\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}-2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

The corresponding system is now

$$
{\begin{aligned}x+3y=1 \\ 0x+0y=1.\end{aligned}
$$

However, the final equation $0x+0y=1$ has no solution. It simplifies to $0=1,$ which is a false statement.

So, there is no pair $x,y$ that satisfies both equations in the system. Consequently, the overall system has no solution.

M=[131263]

q-42163.name: Question 9
q-42163.problem:
Consider the system of linear equations

$$
{\begin{aligned}x-3y=2 \\ -12x+36y=-28.\end{aligned}
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to row echelon form, and then find the general solution of the linear system.
q-42163.worked_solution:
First, we set up the augmented matrix for the system:

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & 2 \\ -12 & 36 & -28\end{aligned}]
$$

Reducing $M$ to row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & 2 \\ -12 & 36 & -28\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+12{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & -4\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

The corresponding system is now

$$
{\begin{aligned}x-3y=2 \\ 0x+0y=-4.\end{aligned}
$$

However, the final equation $0x+0y=-4$ has no solution. It simplifies to $0=-4,$ which is a false statement.

So, there is no pair $x,y$ that satisfies both equations in the system. Consequently, the overall system has no solution.

q-20961.name: Question 10
q-20961.problem:
Consider the system of linear equations

$$
{\begin{aligned}2x+6y=10 \\ 3x+9y=21.\end{aligned}
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to row echelon form, and then find the general solution of the linear system.
q-20961.worked_solution:
First, we set up the augmented matrix for the system:

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}2 & 6 & 10 \\ 3 & 9 & 21\end{aligned}]
$$

Reducing $M$ to row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}2 & 6 & 10 \\ 3 & 9 & 21\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=\frac{1}{2}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 5 \\ 3 & 9 & 21\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}-3{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 5 \\ 0 & 0 & 6\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

The corresponding system is now

$$
{\begin{aligned}x+3y=5 \\ 0x+0y=6.\end{aligned}
$$

However, the final equation $0x+0y=6$ has no solution. It simplifies to $0=6,$ which is a false statement.

So, there is no pair $x,y$ that satisfies both equations in the system. Consequently, the overall system has no solution.

Consider the system of linear equations {2x+6y=103x+9y=21. Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix M of the system to row echelon form, and then find the general solution of the linear system.

EXPLANATION

First, we set up the augmented matrix for the system: M=[26103921]

Reducing M to row echelon form, we have M∼[26103921]R1:=12R1∼[1353921]R2:=R2−3R1∼[135006].

The corresponding system is now {x+3y=50x+0y=6.

However, the final equation 0x+0y=6 has no solution. It simplifies to 0=6, which is a false statement.

So, there is no pair x,y that satisfies both equations in the system. Consequently, the overall system has no solution.
